The best free inventory management software

Free inventory plans are usually a taster: a cap on items or orders, one user, and the useful parts such as stock counts and alerts on a paid plan. Here is what each one gives for free, from its own pages.

We make Slop Inventory, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • What the free plan allows: items, orders, users, locations
  • Barcode scanning, stock counts and low-stock alerts on the free plan
  • Orders and purchasing
  • Account needed, and where the stock data is kept

1. Slop Inventory (ours)

Best for: A small shop or workshop that wants counts, locations and reorder alerts free, on one computer

Products and stock by location in the browser: scan with the camera or a USB scanner, receive, move and count stock, set reorder levels, and see the stock value, with orders and purchase orders in the sibling apps.

Good

  • No limit on products, locations or movements
  • Stock counts, transfers, reorder levels and a low-stock list free
  • CSV import with a validation report, and CSV export
  • Fulfilled orders take stock out (Slop Orders); received purchase orders put it back (Slop Purchases)
  • Works on your phone, tablet and computer in the browser, even offline

Not so good

  • Camera scanning needs a Chromium-based browser (the browser's BarcodeDetector)
  • No item photos, no custom fields, no barcode labels
  • One person in one browser: no team, no sync between devices
  • Still being built

Open Slop Inventory

2. Sortly

Best for: Visual tracking of a small number of items with photos and a phone app

Good

  • Item photos, folders, tags and inventory import on the free plan
  • Barcode and QR scanning with the phone, and offline mobile access with automatic sync
  • Activity history and inventory summary reports

Not so good

  • Free plan: 100 unique items and one user
  • Low-stock alerts, QR labels and check-in/check-out need Advanced; barcode labels, stock counts and purchase orders need Ultra
  • Third-party scanners from Ultra up

Sortly website · Sources: Sortly pricing and plan table

3. Zoho Inventory (Free)

Best for: Selling products with sales orders, kits and dropshipping at a very small scale

Good

  • Composite items, dropshipping and backorders on the free plan
  • Integrations with 3PL providers, Zoho apps, Slack and more
  • Mobile and Windows apps

Not so good

  • Free plan: 50 orders, one user and one location
  • Stock counting, barcode generation and serial or batch tracking are on Premium ($79)
  • Customer portal starts on Standard

Zoho Inventory (Free) website · Sources: Zoho Inventory pricing

Which one to choose

Slop Inventory is our pick when the free plan has to do real stock control: counts, locations and reorder alerts with no item cap, installable from the browser and usable offline. It is for one person, without photos or labels.

Choose Sortly for a small, visual inventory with item photos on a phone, within 100 items. Choose Zoho Inventory for a business selling online that will grow into its paid plans; its free plan stops at 50 orders and one location.

Questions

Is there free inventory software with no item limit?

Of these, Slop Inventory sets no limit. Sortly's free plan allows 100 unique items; Zoho Inventory's free plan is limited to 50 orders and one location.

Can I scan barcodes for free?

Sortly includes barcode and QR scanning with the phone on its free plan. Slop Inventory reads codes from any USB scanner, and from the camera in Chromium-based browsers.

Which free inventory software does stock counts?

Slop Inventory includes stock counts free. On Sortly they are an Ultra feature and on Zoho Inventory a Premium feature, as their pricing pages show.

Where is my stock data kept?

Sortly and Zoho Inventory keep it on their services. Slop Inventory keeps it in your browser on this device; download a backup to keep a copy.
